newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Foreign investment in China seen likely to jump.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in China seen likely to jump.

text.p: China will experience a take-off period in foreign investment in 1997, Arthur Ansersen, one of the world leading consultant firms, said on Thursday.
"In looking ahead, foreign investors should see 1997 as a good year to make new or additional investments in China," Nellie Fong, the firm's deputy managing partner for China, said in a statement.

"Because China's domestic market is more open to foreign investments, inflation is under control, the yuan is relatively stable and is backed by strong foreign reserves, and the country's projected growth rate of eight to nine percent over the next five years, under the ninth Five-Year Plan from 1996 to 2000, offers many new opportunities," she said.

Fong, who is also the executive committee chairman of Better Hong Kong Foundation, said that China's foreign reserves of US$90 billion and the relative opening up of the services sector were also positive to investment.
The Better Hong Kong Foundation is a billionaires' club in promoting the territory before and after the transfer of Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty in 1997.

Foreign investments in China rose 17 percent in the first nine months of this year, up from US$24.9 billion to US$29.9 billion. The upward trend was spurred by continuous attractive economic environment that had emerged in China.
